headline: ChatGPT swaps text for visual answers with GPT-6
dek: A new interface builds diagrams and calculators in the chat, per TechCrunch and Canaltech.

s2.label: What happened
s2.title: Less text, more visuals
body: OpenAI began rolling out Intelligent UI, a new ChatGPT interface that launches alongside the GPT-6 model (TechCrunch, Canaltech).
Answers can now include tappable buttons, custom calculators, editable charts and diagrams that users manipulate inside the chat (TechCrunch, Canaltech).

s3.label: How it works
s3.title: The screen is built with the answer
s3.body: The system assembles visual components while it writes, instead of writing text first and illustrating it later (Canaltech).

points.t: In a press demo, a question about how a wing generates lift became a set of interactive diagrams (TechCrunch, Canaltech).
A request involving math can generate a tool built for that specific problem, per Canaltech.
Users who prefer text can reduce the visual elements in ChatGPT's settings (TechCrunch, Canaltech).

s4.label: Why it matters
s4.title: Who gets it first
body: Pro, Plus, Business and Enterprise subscribers got it first, running GPT-6 Sol. Free and Go accounts use GPT-6 Luna (Canaltech).
For now it stays in the chat tab, not in Work or Codex. On Enterprise, admins control availability (Canaltech).

stat.cap: rollout to Free and Go accounts (TechCrunch)

items.t: OpenAI showed a bicycle mechanics diagram, a recipe walkthrough and a financial simulator (TechCrunch, Canaltech).
TechCrunch says the change could bring ChatGPT a wider audience. OpenAI did not say so.
OpenAI says the model got faster, searches the web better and resists jailbreaks more (Canaltech).

caption.hook: The ChatGPT visual interface arrived with GPT-6: answers now come with diagrams, calculators and editable charts.
body: OpenAI product manager Aarush Selvan said the most helpful answers "aren't just text," according to TechCrunch. The company wants to help with everyday tasks, from planning a trip to learning a new subject.
Intelligent UI reached paid subscribers on Wednesday, October 7, and Free and Go accounts on Thursday, per TechCrunch and Canaltech. Users who prefer plain text can turn the visuals down in settings.
caption.cta: Which everyday task would you rather see as a diagram than as text in ChatGPT?
